# bide-hsm command reference

<!-- Generated by TestReference in cmd/bide/bide-hsm from what the commands print for -h. Do not edit:
     run go test . -run TestReference -update in cmd/bide/bide-hsm. CI fails when this page is stale. -->

bide-hsm is [bide approve](cli.md#bide-approve) for approvers whose signing keys are in an HSM, on a
smart card or token, or in a cloud KMS. It is a separate program because the PKCS#11 library it loads
needs cgo, and the `bide` command is built without it. It is not in the release archives: build it
from source (it needs a C compiler for PKCS#11 keys; without cgo it builds and still signs with a KMS key):

```sh
CGO_ENABLED=1 go install github.com/bide-ai/bide/cmd/bide/bide-hsm@latest
```

Key custody is explained in [the key custody guide](../guides/key-custody.md#approver-keys); the
approval flow in [Human approval](../guides/hitl-approval.md). Flags take one dash, as in `bide`.
Exit status is 0 for success, 1 for a refusal or a failure, and 2 for a usage error.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`bide-hsm approve`](#bide-hsm-approve) | record your signed approval (or -reject) of a call that waits for a decision, with a key in an HSM or KMS; -list shows what waits |
| [`bide-hsm pubkey`](#bide-hsm-pubkey) | print the public key of a key in an HSM or KMS, and the approver-keys entry that enrols it |
| [`bide-hsm version`](#bide-hsm-version) | print the version and whether this build can use PKCS#11 keys |

## bide-hsm approve

```text
bide-hsm approve: record a signed approval, or a rejection, of a call that waits for a decision,
with a key in an HSM or a KMS

  bide-hsm approve -db <file> -run <id> -call <tool-use id> -as <approver> -key <key ref> -approver-keys <keys> [flags]
  bide-hsm approve -postgres-env <VAR> -run <id> -call <tool-use id> -as <approver> -key <key ref> -approver-keys <keys>
  bide-hsm approve -db <file> -list

This is bide approve (see bide approve -h, and the bide command reference) with one difference:
-key is a reference to a key that stays in an HSM or a KMS, not a key file. Everything else is the
same code: what it shows, the confirmation, the checks that refuse, -approver-keys, -unverified,
-reject, -yes, -full, -list, -json, -verify-receipt, the exit status (0 on success, 1 if it
refused or failed, 2 for a usage error). Two differences follow from the key: a default receipt is
written in the working directory (there is no key file to put it beside), and the HSM or KMS is
opened (a PKCS#11 login; for KMS, one billed self-test signature) after the checks on the gate
pass and before you are asked to confirm, so that the key shown is the key that signs. The
decision itself is signed only after you confirm. A refusal on the gate (you are not an approver,
you already decided the other way) and a repeat of a decision that already counts happen before
the key is opened.

A key reference is one of:

  pkcs11:token=<label>;object=<label>?module-path=<absolute path>&pin-source=file:/path
      An RFC 7512 PKCS#11 URI, for a key in an HSM or on a smart card or token. token (or
      slot-id) selects the token; object (the key's label), id (its CKA_ID as percent-encoded
      bytes) or both select the key; module-path is the vendor's PKCS#11 library, loaded and run
      by this program, so name only a library you trust. The PIN is read from
      pin-source=file:/absolute/path (on Unix the file must not be readable by others) or
      pin-source=env:NAME, or asked for on the controlling terminal with echo off by
      pin-source=prompt (never read from a pipe; refused when there is no terminal), or typed on
      the token's own PIN pad by pin-source=protected (the token must report a protected
      authentication path, else it is refused; needs -alg, as each login asks on the pad), and with
      no pin-source from $BIDE_HSM_PIN. The PIN is never part of the
      reference: pin-value is refused, and so is every attribute not listed here (serial,
      manufacturer, module-name, ...), not ignored, since an ignored attribute would let a
      reference select a key more loosely than it reads. Percent-encode ; ? & = % and spaces in a
      value, and quote the whole reference in a shell, which treats ; and & as operators.
  awskms:arn:aws:kms:<region>:<account>:key/<id>
      An AWS KMS key by its full ARN (alias/<name> in place of key/<id> names an alias, which is
      resolved once). Credentials come from the AWS SDK's default chain (environment, shared
      config, instance or task role); the ARN's region is used.
  gcpkms:projects/<p>/locations/<l>/keyRings/<r>/cryptoKeys/<k>/cryptoKeyVersions/<n>
      A Google Cloud KMS key version by its full resource name with the numeric version (no alias,
      no "latest": signing uses exactly that version). Credentials are Google's application default
      credentials. Only an HSM-backed version is used unless -allow-software-key (Cloud KMS has no
      HSM-backed Ed25519 key, so an Ed25519 key needs it, and approve then says so beside the key);
      -verify-attestation requires the key's Cloud HSM attestation to prove it was generated in the
      HSM and cannot be extracted.

The key is Ed25519 or ECDSA P-256, the schemes HSMs and KMS sign; -alg names the scheme, and
without it the key's type is detected. A PKCS#11 key must be marked non-extractable and sensitive
by the token, or it is refused, since a key that can be read out of the token defeats keeping it
there; -allow-extractable lifts that, and bide-hsm approve then says so beside the key. The token
or KMS signs; bide-hsm never holds the private key.

Flags:
  -alg string
    	the key's scheme: ed25519 or ecdsa-p256 (default: detect it)
  -allow-extractable
    	use a PKCS#11 key the token does not mark non-extractable and sensitive; by default such a key is refused
  -allow-software-key
    	use a Google Cloud KMS key version at protection level SOFTWARE; by default only an HSM-backed version is used, and Cloud KMS has no HSM-backed Ed25519 key
  -approver-keys string
    	approver public keys, a JSON object of approver id to key text, e.g. {"ops":"ed25519:ab12..."}, the file bide view -approver-keys reads (bide-hsm pubkey -as prints an entry): refuse a -key that is not the one enrolled for -as, and verify the tally. Required for an m-of-n gate unless -unverified
  -as string
    	your approver id, exactly as the gate's policy lists it (not for a single-approver gate)
  -call string
    	the call's tool-use ID (for a plan flow node, its key, such as node:review)
  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never
  -db string
    	SQLite journal file
  -full
    	show all of the call's arguments, not the first lines
  -json
    	with -list: print the waiting calls as JSON
  -key string
    	reference to your key in an HSM or KMS: a pkcs11: URI (RFC 7512; quote it), awskms:<key ARN> or gcpkms:<key version>; not for a single-approver gate
  -list
    	list the calls that wait for a decision, each with its bide-hsm approve command; nothing is recorded
  -postgres string
    	Postgres journal, a pgx DSN such as postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db; prefer -postgres-env, which keeps the password out of the argument list
  -postgres-env string
    	name of the environment variable that holds the Postgres DSN
  -receipt string
    	where to write the decision receipt (default: in the working directory, named <run>-<call>-<approver>-<time>.receipt.json); mode 0600, never overwritten
  -reject
    	record a rejection instead of an approval
  -run string
    	the run whose journal holds the call: the pause's run ID
  -unverified
    	decide an m-of-n gate without -approver-keys: the key is not checked against the one enrolled for you, and the tally is not verified
  -verify-attestation
    	for a Google Cloud KMS key version in an HSM, require its Cloud HSM attestation to prove the key was generated there and cannot be extracted
  -verify-receipt string
    	verify a decision receipt on its own, against -approver-keys, instead of deciding anything: its signature over the exact call it states
  -yes
    	do not ask for confirmation (for scripts); what is signed is still shown
```

## bide-hsm pubkey

```text
usage: bide-hsm pubkey -key <key ref> [-as <approver id>] [-alg ed25519|ecdsa-p256] [-allow-extractable]

Prints the public key of a key in an HSM or a KMS, in the form approval policies and verifiers read
(<scheme>:<hex>), and with -as the entry for the JSON object bide approve -approver-keys and bide
view -approver-keys read: {"ops": "<scheme>:<hex>"}. Enroll that key in the application that runs
the gated agent, and in the file approvers pass as -approver-keys.

It opens the key as bide-hsm approve does, so it needs the PIN (a PKCS#11 key) or the credentials
(a KMS key), checks that the key can sign, and refuses what approve refuses. For a KMS key that
check is one signature, billed as one KMS request. The private key is never read out.

A key reference is one of:

  pkcs11:token=<label>;object=<label>?module-path=<absolute path>&pin-source=file:/path
      An RFC 7512 PKCS#11 URI, for a key in an HSM or on a smart card or token. token (or
      slot-id) selects the token; object (the key's label), id (its CKA_ID as percent-encoded
      bytes) or both select the key; module-path is the vendor's PKCS#11 library, loaded and run
      by this program, so name only a library you trust. The PIN is read from
      pin-source=file:/absolute/path (on Unix the file must not be readable by others) or
      pin-source=env:NAME, or asked for on the controlling terminal with echo off by
      pin-source=prompt (never read from a pipe; refused when there is no terminal), or typed on
      the token's own PIN pad by pin-source=protected (the token must report a protected
      authentication path, else it is refused; needs -alg, as each login asks on the pad), and with
      no pin-source from $BIDE_HSM_PIN. The PIN is never part of the
      reference: pin-value is refused, and so is every attribute not listed here (serial,
      manufacturer, module-name, ...), not ignored, since an ignored attribute would let a
      reference select a key more loosely than it reads. Percent-encode ; ? & = % and spaces in a
      value, and quote the whole reference in a shell, which treats ; and & as operators.
  awskms:arn:aws:kms:<region>:<account>:key/<id>
      An AWS KMS key by its full ARN (alias/<name> in place of key/<id> names an alias, which is
      resolved once). Credentials come from the AWS SDK's default chain (environment, shared
      config, instance or task role); the ARN's region is used.
  gcpkms:projects/<p>/locations/<l>/keyRings/<r>/cryptoKeys/<k>/cryptoKeyVersions/<n>
      A Google Cloud KMS key version by its full resource name with the numeric version (no alias,
      no "latest": signing uses exactly that version). Credentials are Google's application default
      credentials. Only an HSM-backed version is used unless -allow-software-key (Cloud KMS has no
      HSM-backed Ed25519 key, so an Ed25519 key needs it, and approve then says so beside the key);
      -verify-attestation requires the key's Cloud HSM attestation to prove it was generated in the
      HSM and cannot be extracted.

The key is Ed25519 or ECDSA P-256, the schemes HSMs and KMS sign; -alg names the scheme, and
without it the key's type is detected. A PKCS#11 key must be marked non-extractable and sensitive
by the token, or it is refused, since a key that can be read out of the token defeats keeping it
there; -allow-extractable lifts that, and bide-hsm approve then says so beside the key. The token
or KMS signs; bide-hsm never holds the private key.

Flags:
  -alg string
    	the key's scheme: ed25519 or ecdsa-p256 (default: detect it)
  -allow-extractable
    	use a PKCS#11 key the token does not mark non-extractable and sensitive; by default such a key is refused
  -allow-software-key
    	use a Google Cloud KMS key version at protection level SOFTWARE; by default only an HSM-backed version is used, and Cloud KMS has no HSM-backed Ed25519 key
  -as string
    	the approver id the key is for: prints the approver-keys entry for it
  -color when
    	when to color the output: auto (the default: on a terminal, unless NO_COLOR is set or TERM is dumb), always or never
  -key string
    	reference to the key: a pkcs11: URI (quote it), awskms:<key ARN> or gcpkms:<key version>
  -verify-attestation
    	for a Google Cloud KMS key version in an HSM, require its Cloud HSM attestation to prove the key was generated there and cannot be extracted
```

## bide-hsm version

```text
usage: bide-hsm version
```

Prints `bide-hsm <version>` and whether the build can use PKCS#11 keys (built with cgo) or only KMS keys.

## bide-hsm help

```text
bide-hsm: bide approve for approvers whose keys are in an HSM or a cloud KMS

  bide-hsm approve -db <file> -run <id> -call <tool-use id> -as <approver> -key <key ref> -approver-keys <keys> [flags]
  bide-hsm approve -db <file> -list
  bide-hsm pubkey  -key <key ref> [-as <approver>]
  bide-hsm version

bide-hsm approve is bide approve, with -key naming a key by reference instead of a key file. It
reads the call from the journal, shows what it will sign, asks you to confirm, has the HSM or KMS
sign the decision, checks it against the call, records it, and writes a receipt.
bide-hsm pubkey prints the approver-keys entry that enrols a key. Each command takes -h.

A key reference is one of:

  pkcs11:token=<label>;object=<label>?module-path=<absolute path>&pin-source=file:/path
      An RFC 7512 PKCS#11 URI, for a key in an HSM or on a smart card or token. token (or
      slot-id) selects the token; object (the key's label), id (its CKA_ID as percent-encoded
      bytes) or both select the key; module-path is the vendor's PKCS#11 library, loaded and run
      by this program, so name only a library you trust. The PIN is read from
      pin-source=file:/absolute/path (on Unix the file must not be readable by others) or
      pin-source=env:NAME, or asked for on the controlling terminal with echo off by
      pin-source=prompt (never read from a pipe; refused when there is no terminal), or typed on
      the token's own PIN pad by pin-source=protected (the token must report a protected
      authentication path, else it is refused; needs -alg, as each login asks on the pad), and with

      reference: pin-value is refused, and so is every attribute not listed here (serial,

      reference select a key more loosely than it reads. Percent-encode ; ? & = % and spaces in a
      value, and quote the whole reference in a shell, which treats ; and & as operators.
  awskms:arn:aws:kms:<region>:<account>:key/<id>
      An AWS KMS key by its full ARN (alias/<name> in place of key/<id> names an alias, which is
      resolved once). Credentials come from the AWS SDK's default chain (environment, shared
      config, instance or task role); the ARN's region is used.
  gcpkms:projects/<p>/locations/<l>/keyRings/<r>/cryptoKeys/<k>/cryptoKeyVersions/<n>
      A Google Cloud KMS key version by its full resource name with the numeric version (no alias,

      HSM-backed Ed25519 key, so an Ed25519 key needs it, and approve then says so beside the key);
      -verify-attestation requires the key's Cloud HSM attestation to prove it was generated in the
      HSM and cannot be extracted.

The key is Ed25519 or ECDSA P-256, the schemes HSMs and KMS sign; -alg names the scheme, and
without it the key's type is detected. A PKCS#11 key must be marked non-extractable and sensitive

```
